question.problem:
Suppose we wish to find a zero of the function $f(x,y)$ in the region $[-3,-1]\times [1,3]⊆{R}^{2},$ where $$ f(x,y)=[\begin{aligned}x{y}^{3}-y+7 \\ {x}^{3}-xy+1\end{aligned}]. $$ Fill in the blanks in the matrix equation below that defines the first iteration of the Newton-Raphson process starting at the point $[-1,\,2]^{T},$ and compute the components of the first iteration, rounding your final answer to three decimal places (if needed).
$[$ $8$ {{field-1}} $]({x}_{1}-{x}_{0})\,=[$ {{field-2}} $]$
{{field-3}} $1$ $-2$
${x}_{1}≈[$ $-2.095$ $]$
{{field-4}}
question.worked_solution:
The Newton-Raphson method of finding the zeros of a multivariable function $f:{R}^{n}\to {R}^{n}$ is

$$
{x}_{n+1}={x}_{n}-[{J}_{f}({x}_{n})]^{-1}f({x}_{n}),
$$

where ${J}_{f}({x}_{n})$ is the Jacobian of $f$ evaluated at ${x}_{n}.$

Equivalently, at each iteration, the above equation can be re-written as 

$$
{J}_{f}({x}_{n})({x}_{n+1}-{x}_{n})=-f({x}_{n}).
$$

In our case, the Jacobian is

$$
\begin{aligned}{J}_{f}(x) & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂}{∂x}(x{y}^{3}-y+7) & \frac{∂}{∂y}(x{y}^{3}-y+7) \\ \frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{3}-xy+1) & \frac{∂}{∂y}({x}^{3}-xy+1)\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}{y}^{3} & 3x{y}^{2}-1 \\ 3{x}^{2}-y & -x\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, our Newton-Raphson system of equations is

$$
{[\begin{aligned}{y}^{3} & 3x{y}^{2} \\ 3{x}^{2}-y & -x\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{n}}({x}_{n+1}-{x}_{n})=-{[\begin{aligned}x{y}^{3}-y+7 \\ {x}^{3}-xy+1\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{n}}.
$$

Starting with ${x}_{0}=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 2\end{aligned}],$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{[\begin{aligned}{y}^{3} & 3x{y}^{2}-1 \\ 3{x}^{2}-y & -x\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{0}}({x}_{1}-{x}_{0}) & =-{[\begin{aligned}x{y}^{3}-y+7 \\ {x}^{3}-xy+1\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{0}} \\ [\begin{aligned}{2}^{3} & 3(-1)(2)^{2}-1 \\ 3(-1)^{2}-2 & -(-1)\end{aligned}]({x}_{1}-{x}_{0}) & =-[\begin{aligned}(-1)(2)^{3}-2+7 \\ (-1)^{3}-(-1)(2)+1\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}8 & -13 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}]({x}_{1}-{x}_{0}) & =[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Solving this system of equations, we get $({x}_{1}-{x}_{0})=[\begin{aligned}-\frac{23}{21} \\ -\frac{19}{21}\end{aligned}].$ Hence,

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & ={x}_{0}+[\begin{aligned}-\frac{23}{21} \\ -\frac{19}{21}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 2\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}-\frac{23}{21} \\ -\frac{19}{21}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-\frac{44}{21} \\ \frac{23}{21}\end{aligned}] \\  & ≈[\begin{aligned}-2.095 \\ 1.095\end{aligned}],\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to three decimal places.
